messages:
Emily Zhao: Heads-up — Customer #2482 reporting intermittent 401s + ~700ms p95. Their console shows region=eu-west but our serving logs show requests landing in us-central. They’re worried about auth scope + cross-region egress billing. Ticket attached: https://support.redwood.ai/t/2482

Raj Patel: Can you paste the sample request they’re sending? do we have any trace ids?

Emily Zhao: Copied from user (redacted token):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-user-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","input":"hello"}'
```
They said console region dropdown was eu-west and they pinned model to eu-west. Trace ids from their Customer header: X-Request-ID: rwd-req-20260315-9f2a

Sam Ortiz: I pulled our serving logs for that trace id window. We see route_decision: fallback_to_remote and route_reason: region_resolver_500 for multiple requests. Example log line: 
```
2026-03-15T18:42:11Z trace=rwd-req-20260315-9f2a route_decision=fallback_to_remote route_target=us-central pop_selected=eu-west resolver_status=500 auth_status=OK latency_ms=712
```

Anna Khan: So the resolver returning 500 triggers fallback, which routes to nearest fallback POP (us-central). Why would that trigger 401 for some requests though?

Raj Patel: Two hypotheses: (1) customer token is region-scoped in our auth service and only valid in eu-west auth realm OR (2) the fallback codepath incorrectly strips/changes Authorization header. Need quick repro.

Emily Zhao: I asked the customer to repro with verbose curl. They sent back a failing request where response had 401 and WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="eu-west" header. Full response (redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="eu-west"
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "invalid_token", "message": "token not valid for this realm" }
```

Sam Ortiz: Confirmed on our side: when requests are accepted by the fallback POP, our auth proxy checks token audience/realm and rejects if mismatched. This is expected. The problem is why console still shows eu-west as serving region and why region_resolver is returning 500 intermittently.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3313 — region-resolver errors detected across eu-west cluster, alert threshold crossed.

Raj Patel: Filing as P1 for eng-runtime because this causes auth regressions + billing cross-pop egress. Emily — can you collect the customer’s full request headers + timestamp range? Also add the Console session id so UI team can reproduce the stale label behavior.

Emily Zhao: Provided. Console session id: ui-sess-5e3c. Customer timestamps: 2026-03-15T18:41:50Z -> 2026-03-15T18:43:30Z. I also attached a screenshot where console shows region badge: "eu-west (primary)" while our logs show pop_selected=us-central.

Anna Khan: Engineering note — possible root cause we’ve seen before: a short outage to the region-mapping cache (resolver) caused the control plane to mark eu-west as degraded but UI reads last known desired region from model metadata, not current serving POP. So UI displays configured region while actual runtime falls back. Need fix: surface active serving POP in console and attach a warning if fallback happened.

Raj Patel: For immediate mitigation — propose automatic retry in client SDKs to surface a clearer 401 reason and recommend user to refresh token with global scope. Also ops can whitelist the customer's token across auth-realms as a temporary measure.

Sam Ortiz: Repro steps for eng team:
1) Simulate resolver 500s for eu-west in staging by flipping feature flag "resolver-fail-mode"
2) Send requests pinned to eu-west model version with region header omitted
3) Observe route_decision=fallback_to_remote and auth rejections in fallback POP logs

Sam Ortiz: Logs to look at (staging): 
- /var/log/serving/pop-routing.log
- /var/log/auth-proxy/realm-check.log

Emily Zhao: Customer has temporarily rotated token to a global-scoped key and reports errors gone. They’re asking for root cause and an ETA for a console/UI change that avoids confusion.

Anna Khan: Action items:
- eng-runtime: investigate resolver 500s and fix resilience (Raj)
- eng-platform: add explicit serving-pop badge to Console and warn on fallback (Sam)
- support: propose rollback steps and temporary auth whitelist (Emily)
- billing: check cross-pop egress for customer #2482 during the window (Anna)

Raj Patel: Assigning INC-2026-3313 to eng-runtime on-call. I’ll add a short postmortem template and link here once we have root cause.

Emily Zhao: Thanks — will update customer with mitigation and ask them to re-open if they see new 401s. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INC-2026-3313 status -> acknowledged by eng-runtime.

Anna Khan: Follow-up: discovered a race in resolver cache refresh where a TTL refresh failing returns 500 instead of using stale map. Priority bug: RESOLVER-712.

Raj Patel: RESOLVER-712 assigned, target patch in next hotfix cycle (ETA 8h). UI change tracked under CONSOLE-324.

Emily Zhao: I'll close out the ticket once patches land and billing confirms no further cross-region charge.

Anna Khan: Thanks team.
